title: Simulation of Thermofluids and Fluid Dynamics using Julia

Simulation of Thermofluids and Fluid Dynamics using Julia


A master-level engineering lecture combining classical thermofluid modeling, numerical simulation, finite differences, finite elements, CFD libraries, machine learning, and physics-informed neural networks.

Formulate thermofluid problems using conservation laws.
Identify suitable models for conduction, convection, advection-diffusion, and incompressible flow.

title: Finite Element Method
text:
3 Gridap.jl Skeleton
using Gridap

domain = (0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
partition = (40, 40)
model = CartesianDiscreteModel(domain, partition)

order = 1
reffe = ReferenceFE(lagrangian, Float64, order)

V = TestFESpace(model, reffe; conformity=:H1)
U = TrialFESpace(V)

Ω = Triangulation(model)
dΩ = Measure(Ω, 2)

k = 1.0

a(T,v) = ∫(k*∇(T)⋅∇(v))dΩ
l(v) = 0

op = AffineFEOperator(a, l, U, V)
T = solve(op)

title: Finite Difference Method
text:
3 Julia Example
using Plots

function heat1d(; L=1.0, Nx=51, α=1e-4, dt=0.1, t_end=100.0)
    dx = L/(Nx-1)
    x = range(0, L, length=Nx)
    Fo = α*dt/dx^2

    T = fill(20.0, Nx)
    T[div(Nx,2)] = 100.0

    Nt = Int(round(t_end/dt))

    for n in 1:Nt
        Tnew = copy(T)
        for i in 2:Nx-1
            Tnew[i] = T[i] + Fo*(T[i+1]-2T[i]+T[i-1])
        end
        Tnew[1] = Tnew[2]
        Tnew[end] = Tnew[end-1]
        T = Tnew
    end

    return x, T
end

x, T = heat1d()
plot(x, T, xlabel="x", ylabel="T")

title: Course Overview
text:
4 Governing Equations

4.1 Heat Conduction
\[
\rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t}
=
\nabla\cdot(k\nabla T)+\dot{q}
\]
For constant \(k\):
\[
\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}
=
\alpha\nabla^2T
+
\frac{\dot{q}}{\rho c_p}
\]


4.2 Incompressible Flow
\[
\nabla\cdot \mathbf{u}=0
\]
\[
\rho
\left(
\frac{\partial \mathbf{u}}{\partial t}
+
\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\mathbf{u}
\right)
=
-\nabla p
+
\mu\nabla^2\mathbf{u}
+
\rho\mathbf{g}
\]


4.3 Energy Equation for Flow
\[
\rho c_p
\left(
\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}
+
\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla T
\right)
=
\nabla\cdot(k\nabla T)+\dot{q}
\]

title: Course Overview
text:
5 Dimensionless Numbers








Number
Definition
Meaning




Reynolds
\(Re=UL/\nu\)
inertia vs. viscosity


Prandtl
\(Pr=\nu/\alpha\)
momentum vs. thermal diffusion


Nusselt
\(Nu=hL/k\)
convective heat transfer


Biot
\(Bi=hL_c/k_s\)
internal vs. external thermal resistance


Fourier
\(Fo=\alpha t/L_c^2\)
dimensionless time


Rayleigh
\(Ra=g\beta\Delta T L^3/(\nu\alpha)\)
natural convection strength

4 Julia Example
using DifferentialEquations
using Plots

function cooling!(du,u,p,t)
    T = u[1]
    Tinf, hA, mcp = p
    du[1] = -hA/mcp*(T-Tinf)
end

u0 = [90.0]
p = (22.0, 0.25, 0.25*4180.0)
prob = ODEProblem(cooling!, u0, (0.0, 3600.0), p)
sol = solve(prob)

plot(sol.t ./ 60, sol[1,:],
     xlabel="Time [min]",
     ylabel="Temperature [°C]",
     label="Coffee")
